No, that is not accurate. In Switzerland, the L-permit (short-stay work permit) is typically required for any work performed within the country, regardless of how short the assignment or the duration of the work. However, the conditions and requirements can vary depending on the type of work, the worker's nationality, and the specific circumstances. 

For a short assignment of two weeks or even a few days once a year, you would generally need to apply for an L-permit. However, the application process and the specific requirements might be simplified or different from those for longer-term assignments. It's always best to consult the official Swiss immigration website or a legal expert to get precise and up-to-date information tailored to your specific situation.
